title: Route Constraints
description: Learn how to constrain route parameters.

data.text: **Route constraints** restrict how parameters are matched in routes. They ensure the correct type and format, preventing invalid URLs from reaching your actions.
Constraints are added inline to route parameters using a colon, for example `{id:int}`. They can check type, length, range, or match a regular expression.

data.title: Constraints

terms.definition: A rule added to a route parameter that restricts which values match the route.
Limits a parameter to a specific type, such as int, bool, or datetime.
Limits a numeric parameter to a minimum or maximum value.
Matches a parameter against a custom regular expression pattern.

data.title: 404 for Invalid Routes
data.text: If a route constraint doesn't match, ASP.NET Core returns 404 automatically.

data.title: Add the Right Constraint
data.description: For each route parameter, choose the appropriate constraint so invalid values are rejected.
steps: Identify the parameter's expected type (int, string, bool)
Add a type constraint if the value must be numeric or alphabetic
Add a min/max range constraint for numeric bounds
Use a regex constraint for custom formats like postal codes
data.expectedOutcome: Routes that reject non-integer IDs and out-of-range values, returning 404 instead of reaching the action.

items.text: Use type constraints for int, bool, and datetime
items.hint: Prevents type-mismatch errors before they reach your action.

items.text: Apply min/max range constraints to numeric parameters
items.hint: Rejects values outside valid business ranges.
Ideal for codes, slugs, and identifiers.
Constraints are part of the routing pipeline, not model validation.
